analysis: The overnight change versus the 4am brief: futures held near-flat to slightly higher (S&P +0.06-0.12%, Dow +0.1%, Nasdaq 100 -0.05 to -0.2%) — the weekend AI-safety overhang didn't deepen, but Asia chip weakness (KOSPI -2.21%, SOXX premarket -1.5% after a 5% down week) shows the AI-capex question is the market's unresolved worry. Oil is the noisiest tape: prints across pages disagree on both level and direction (WTI $91-93, Brent $103-107), which tells you the ceasefire headline isn't tradeable yet — one outlet's drop is another's rally, and with Russia unconfirmed and Zelensky rejecting it, the story is fragile. The dollar at an 18-month high plus a 5.24% 10Y says macro is still pricing inflation risk into Wednesday's CPI. Earnings expectations (29-31% growth) set a demanding bar: the Deutsche Bank 'above-average beats' call means the numbers alone won't move the tape — guidance on demand, margins, and financing costs will. Signal: bank earnings Tuesday + CPI Wednesday + ASML/TSMC Wed/Thu. Noise: conflicting premarket % prints across auto-generated pages, the stale Tesla-China revenue-share story being recycled, and stale 2025 content (Bitcoin $122K, 401(k) crypto EO) in some auto-aggregator pages.
